headline: CEC real count now at 6.5% of polls (320,750 valid votes)
dek: CEC preliminary count has moved from negligible (15 stations / 2,679 votes at 04:00 scan) to 6.5% of polls reporting, 320,750 valid votes, updated 02:39 Israel time. In that early partial, the Netanyahu bloc leads with 51.3% (164,654 votes) vs opposition bloc 38.4% (123,142) and Arab parties 4.4%…
sources: Israel Central Elections Committee preliminary results as displayed by Poliwave live tracker (poliwave.com/il/live/knesset-2026); exit-poll baseline Channels 12/13/Kan via Reuters
fault_line: Early count puts Netanyahu's bloc ahead -- exit polls said the opposite. Real shift or first-6.5% mirage? And will Eisenkot govern with Arab parties or hand Netanyahu the mandate?

sections.what_happened: CEC preliminary count has moved from negligible (15 stations / 2,679 votes at 04:00 scan) to 6.5% of polls reporting, 320,750 valid votes, updated 02:39 Israel time. In that early partial, the Netanyahu bloc leads with 51.3% (164,654 votes) vs opposition bloc 38.4% (123,142) and Arab parties 4.4% (14,089) -- the REVERSE of the exit-poll bloc order (opposition 52-53, Netanyahu bloc 50, Arab parties 17-18). Poliwave's own seat arithmetic IF the counted votes were final gives Netanyahu bloc 64 / opposition 48 / Arab parties 4 -- that arithmetic is tracker math, NOT an official seat allocation and NOT a forecast, and must never be reported as a result or projection. Exit-poll picture unchanged as the baseline: neither bloc at 61, Likud largest single party (24-25), turnout 77.7%. Eisenkot's election-night line (Times of Israel liveblog, 01:43 Israel time): 'These are still exit poll results, and we must wait for the final count... The public voted for change.'
sections.what_verified: Count numbers: 1 declared-tier family -- the CEC itself (T1 official bodies/primary data class in the registry) as displayed by Poliwave; Poliwave holds NO declared tier and its seat arithmetic does NOT count toward corroboration. Exit-poll baseline: Reuters T1 + Channels 12/13/Kan via Times of Israel T3 (prior scans). Gate: primary_source_single_family=true for the count figures.
sections.what_disputed: Early partials are not representative: 93.5% of polls still to report, and the counted set so far skews to areas reporting first (e.g. Ashdod, Haifa, Lakhish regions lead the tracker table). The Arab-party share in the partial (4.4%) vs exit polls (17-18 seats) shows how unrepresentative the first 6.5% is. thepetek.com still displays its premature 'All ballots counted, Netanyahu bloc 75' page -- contradicted by the CEC tracker itself and already flagged in the 04:00 DNP; never use. A Haaretz page circulating in search ('95% counted, Netanyahu bloc 65') is a 2022-election article, not the 2026 count.
sections.why_matters: The count's first twist: exit polls had Eisenkot ahead -- the first real ballots have Netanyahu's bloc in front. 93.5% still to count; the seat math is not a result yet.
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW UPDATE to totw-20261028-0000-09/0100-01/0200-01/0300-01/0400-01 (Israel election night) -- CEC real count now at 6.5% of polls (320,750 valid votes); early partial LEADS for Netanyahu bloc, reversing exit-poll bloc order, but 93.5% still uncounted

totw_analysis: Our read: The count's first twist: exit polls had Eisenkot ahead -- the first real ballots have Netanyahu's bloc in front. 93.5% still to count; the seat math is not a result yet. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Early count puts Netanyahu's bloc ahead -- exit polls said the opposite. Real shift or first-6.5% mirage? And will Eisenkot govern with Arab parties or hand Netanyahu the mandate?
